docs.title: bdbvhub
docs.text:
Our side of the BDBV Modeling Hub: the model registry, the fit store, the weekly hub file and its checks, and the hub pages of the docs site.

bdbvhub is the package in packages/bdbvhub of the repository (Packages). It sits at the top of the package stack and imports every other nowcast* package. Its bdbvhub command is what the CI workflows call.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv pip install "git+https://github.com/seabbs/bdbv-hub-modelling#subdirectory=packages/bdbvhub"

From a clone of the repository, uv sync --package bdbvhub installs it with the packages it needs.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
A model returns sample trajectories: one row per province, week and sample. We make three samples of two weeks for two provinces.

import pandas as pd

samples = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        (location, week, sample, value + sample)
        for location, value in (("CD-KN", 4), ("CD-NK", 10))
        for week in ("2026-03-14", "2026-03-21")
        for sample in (1, 2, 3)
    ],
    columns=["location", "target_end_date", "sample", "value"],
)

to_hub_table lays them out as the hub's submission table. It checks that every place has the same sample ids and weeks, and adds the country (CD) as the sum of its provinces, sample by sample.

from bdbvhub.submission.hub import HUB_COLUMNS, to_hub_table

table = to_hub_table(
    samples, "2026-03-14", n_samples=3, forecast_date="2026-03-14"
)
assert tuple(table.columns) == HUB_COLUMNS
national = table.query("location == 'CD'")
assert national["value"].tolist() == [16, 16, 18, 18, 20, 20]

A hub model id joins our team abbreviation and the model's, and the file goes under model-output/<model id>/.

import tempfile

from bdbvhub.submission.hub import model_id, write_submission

mid = model_id("rwnowcast")
assert mid == "seabbs-rwnowcast"
out = tempfile.mkdtemp()
path = write_submission(table, out, mid)
assert path.name == "2026-03-14-seabbs-rwnowcast.csv"

docs.title: Find the registered models
docs.text:
Importing bdbvhub.models registers every built-in model: the random walks, the Chronos-2 models and the renewal variants. get_model builds one by name.

from bdbvhub.models import list_models

names = {spec.name for spec in list_models()}
assert {"randomwalk", "randomwalknowcast", "renewal", "foundation"} <= names

docs.title: Look up a submission fit configuration
docs.text:
The submission CI fits each candidate in its fallback chain with bdbvhub fit --config <name>. Each name maps to a FitConfig that says how to fit the model and how to forecast from the fit.

from bdbvhub.submission.fitting import get_config

config = get_config("randomwalk")
assert config.name == "randomwalk"
print(config.description)

docs.title: Check a submission file name
docs.text:
The hub reads the round, team and model from each file name. parse_file_name splits a name as the hub's own checks do.

from bdbvhub.submission.validate import parse_file_name

parts = parse_file_name(path.name)
assert parts == {
    "round_id": "2026-03-14",
    "team": "seabbs",
    "model": "rwnowcast",
    "ext": "csv",
}

validate_file runs the full checks against a local clone of the hub (Hub.load), as bdbvhub validate does.

docs.title: Build model metadata
docs.text:
render_model_metadata builds a model's metadata record in the hub's field order, with our team's shared fields filled in. MODEL_METADATA holds the text of each model that may be submitted.

from bdbvhub.submission.hub import render_model_metadata
from bdbvhub.submission.metadata import MODEL_METADATA

record = render_model_metadata("randomwalk", **MODEL_METADATA["randomwalk"])
assert record["team_abbr"] == "seabbs"
assert record["model_abbr"] == "randomwalk"

docs.title: Label weeks a fallback went out under our hub id
docs.text:
When the first model in the chain fails its checks, a fallback goes out under the same hub id. split_substituted gives those weeks their own label so the comparison with the hub can show them apart.

from bdbvhub.compare import split_substituted

forecasts = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "model": ["seabbs-renewal", "seabbs-renewal"],
        "reference_date": ["2026-03-07", "2026-03-14"],
    }
)
ledger = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "reference_date": ["2026-03-14"],
        "hub_id": ["seabbs-renewal"],
        "model": ["renewalsp"],
        "substituted": ["true"],
    }
)
relabelled = split_substituted(forecasts, ledger)
assert relabelled["model"].tolist() == [
    "seabbs-renewal",
    "seabbs-renewal [renewalsp]",
]

docs.title: bdbvhub.models
docs.text:
The model registry, with every built-in model registered.

The models live in their own packages: the random walks in nowcastbaselines.randomwalk, Chronos-2 in nowcastfoundation.forecaster, and the renewal variants in nowcastrenewal.forecaster and nowcastrenewal.zones. The registry itself is nowcastutils.base.

Importing this module registers the built-in models, so look models up here (get_model, list_models). To add a variant, write a class with name and forecast(task), call register_model in its module, then import that module here.

docs.title: bdbvhub.cli
docs.text:
Command line interface: bdbvhub <command>.

Commands:

  • data: download the hub data and write the tidy tables.
  • backtest: run the development backtest, or with --lopo the leave-one-province-out check.
  • nowcast: forecast from a real vintage, write the hub file and check it. With --config (and --fit), forecast from a fit configuration.
  • zone-backtest: score the random walks' stored zone runs.
  • digest: hash what a backtest reads, to key its cached outputs.
  • concat-results: stack the results files of runs made apart.
  • score: score the forecasts of --forecast-only runs together.
  • fit: fit a configuration and write the fit directory and its diagnostics.json, for the submission CI.
  • fit-store: list the fitted models' fits the store lacks, make one, load the stored fits into the results (bdbvhub.store.store), or archive every candidate's forecasts for a round (bdbvhub.store.archive).
  • plot-submission: plot a submitted hub file.
  • plot-rt-submission: plot the wk R_t rows of a submitted hub file.
  • plot-ppc: plot a fit's posterior predictive checks (ppc.json).
  • coherence: compare the national data with the sum of the provinces.
  • rt-check: write the Rt sense-check page of a renewal fit directory (bdbvhub.reporting.rtcheck).
  • validate: run the hub's checks on files (submission.validate).
  • metadata: write and check a model's metadata YAML.
  • finetuned-checkpoint: print the settings hash of the fine-tuned checkpoint the _ft models load, resolved once for a run's jobs.
  • compare-hub: score our forecasts against the hub's submitted ones.
  • report: make the docs figures and tables.

--version prints the package version. Paths to the tidy data default to $BDBV_DATA_DIR or data/, so the submission CI can point every command at the data it pinned.

def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run the command line interface.

    Parameters
    ----------
    argv : sequence of str, optional
        Arguments. Defaults to `sys.argv[1:]`.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Exit status.

    Examples
    --------
    From the shell, download the data, forecast with the random walk
    nowcast and write its hub file under `output/submission/`:

        bdbvhub data
        bdbvhub nowcast --model randomwalknowcast --vintage latest
        bdbvhub <command> --help

    The same from Python:

    >>> from bdbvhub.cli import main
    >>> main(["nowcast", "--model", "randomwalknowcast", "--vintage", "latest"])
    """
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    # JAX logs its backend search at INFO, which is noise here.
    logging.getLogger("jax").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    if argv[:1] == ["validate"]:
        return validate_main(argv[1:])
    # For loaders called with no directory, as inside a renewal fit.
    tidy._DEFAULT_DATA_DIR = _data_root()
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.version:
        print(_version())
        return 0
    if args.command is None:
        parser.error("a command is required")
    if args.command == "data":
        fetch_hub_data(args.raw, ref=args.ref)
        tables = build_tidy_data(args.raw, args.out)
        print(f"Tidy data written to {args.out} on {dt.date.today()}.")
        target = tables["target"]
        latest = str(target.loc[target["kind"] == "real", "vintage"].max())
        _print_coherence(coherence_summary(target, latest))
        return 0
    if args.command == "fit":
        return _fit(args)
    if args.command == "fit-store":
        if args.action == "archive":
            return _fit_store_archive(args)
        return store.command(args)
    if args.command == "plot-submission":
        return _plot_submission(args)
    if args.command == "coherence":
        return _coherence(args)
    if args.command == "truth-sensitivity":
        from nowcasteval.nowcast import truth_sensitivity, truth_skip

        conf = bt.load_config(args.config)
        target = load_target(args.data)
        got = truth_sensitivity(
            target,
            load_daily(args.data),
            skip=truth_skip(target.query("kind == 'real'"), conf),
        )
        text = (
            got["delays"].to_markdown(index=False)
            + "\n\n"
            + got["complete"].round(3).to_markdown(index=False)
            + "\n"
        )
        if args.out:
            Path(args.out).write_text(text)
        else:
            print(text)
        return 0
    if args.command == "rt-check":
        from bdbvhub.reporting.rtcheck import rt_check_from_fit

        out = Path(args.out)
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(rt_check_from_fit(args.fit, args.data))
        print(f"Wrote {out}")
        return 0
    if args.command == "plot-rt-submission":
        return _plot_rt_submission(args)
    if args.command == "plot-ppc":
        return _plot_ppc(args)
    if args.command == "backtest":
        return _backtest(args)
    if args.command == "nowcast":
        return _nowcast(args)
    if args.command == "zone-backtest":
        return _zone_backtest(args)
    if args.command == "pairing-sensitivity":
        return _pairing_sensitivity(args, str(_data_root()))
    if args.command == "live-checkpoint":
        return _live_checkpoint(args)
    if args.command == "ft-check":
        return _ft_check(args)
    if args.command == "digest":
        from bdbvhub.store.digest import backtest_digest, model_digest

        if args.model:
            print(model_digest(args.model, args.root, args.extra, args.text))
        else:
            print(backtest_digest(args.root, args.extra, args.text))
        return 0
    if args.command == "concat-results":
        return _concat_results(args)
    if args.command == "score":
        return _score(args)
    if args.command == "metadata":
        return _metadata(args)
    if args.command == "bvd":  # pragma: no cover - network
        return _bvd(args)
    if args.command == "finetuned-checkpoint":
        from nowcastfoundation.forecaster import finetuned_checkpoint

        print(finetuned_checkpoint().hash)
        return 0
    if args.command == "hub-id":
        print(model_id(model_abbr_for(args.model, args.hub_toml)))
        return 0
    if args.command == "compare-hub":
        return _compare_hub(args)
    if args.command == "freeze-round":
        from bdbvhub.submission.rounds import freeze_round

        wrote = freeze_round(args.ledger, args.round)
        print(
            f"Round {args.round}: "
            + ("page frozen." if wrote else "already frozen.")
        )
        return 0
    from bdbvhub.reporting.report import make_report

    make_report(
        figures=args.figures,
        generated=args.generated,
        data_dir=_data_root(),
        store=args.store,
    )
    from bdbvhub.submission.rounds import make_round_pages

    done = make_round_pages(args.ledger, generated=args.generated)
    print(f"Round pages: {len(done)} submitted rounds.")
    return 0

def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Build the argument parser.

    Returns
    -------
    argparse.ArgumentParser
        The parser.
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="bdbvhub")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--version", action="store_true", help="Print the version and exit."
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")
    data_dir = str(_data_root())

    data = sub.add_parser("data", help="Download and tidy the hub data.")
    data.add_argument(
        "--raw", default=os.environ.get("BDBV_RAW_DIR", f"{data_dir}/raw")
    )
    data.add_argument("--out", default=data_dir)
    data.add_argument("--ref", default="main")

    back = sub.add_parser("backtest", help="Run the backtest.")
    back.add_argument(
        "--config", default="packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml"
    )
    back.add_argument(
        "--samples",
        type=int,
        help="draws per forecast scored, in place of the config's "
        "[samples] backtest",
    )
    back.add_argument("--data", default=data_dir)
    back.add_argument("--models", nargs="*", default=None)
    back.add_argument("--results", default="results")
    _add_store_arg(back)
    back.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default="results",
        help="Where the forecasts go. The fitted models' rows there come "
        "from the fit store (`fit-store load`) and are kept.",
    )
    back.add_argument(
        "--forecast-only",
        action="store_true",
        help="Forecast without scoring, writing the forecasts to --parts, "
        "so each model can run apart; `score` scores them together.",
    )
    back.add_argument(
        "--parts",
        default="output/parts",
        help="Where --forecast-only writes the forecasts.",
    )
    back.add_argument(
        "--lopo",
        action="store_true",
        help="Run the leave-one-province-out check instead.",
    )

    now = sub.add_parser("nowcast", help="Forecast and write a hub file.")
    now.add_argument(
        "--model",
        default="randomwalk",
        help="Model name. Without --config, the registered model to run.",
    )
    _abbr_args(now)
    _task_args(now, data_dir)
    now.add_argument(
        "--config",
        default=None,
        help="Fit configuration to forecast from, such as `main`.",
    )
    now.add_argument(
        "--fit", default=None, help="Fit directory written by `fit`."
    )
    now.add_argument("--out", default="output/submission")
    now.add_argument(
        "--tasks",
        default=None,
        help="The hub's tasks.json, for the weeks of the wk R_t target "
        "(default: <data>/hub-config/tasks.json).",
    )
    now.add_argument(
        "--forecast-date",
        default=None,
        help="The file's forecast_date. Defaults to today (UTC), the day a "
        "submission's PR is opened.",
    )

    zb = sub.add_parser(
        "zone-backtest",
        help="Score the random walks' zone runs, as the fit store holds "
        "them, on later releases.",
    )
    zb.add_argument("--data", default=data_dir)
    zb.add_argument(
        "--models",
        nargs="*",
        default=["randomwalk", "randomwalknowcast"],
    )
    zb.add_argument(
        "--chunk", default=None, help=_CHUNK_HELP.format(what="origins")
    )
    zb.add_argument(
        "--store",
        default="output/fit-store",
        help="The fit store checkout that `fit-store load` read.",
    )
    zb.add_argument(
        "--results",
        default="results",
        help="Where `fit-store load` wrote its status file, which names "
        "the fits whose zone runs are scored.",
    )
    zb.add_argument("--out", default="results/zone-scores.csv")
    zb.add_argument("--energy-out", default="results/zone-energy.csv")
    zb.add_argument("--quantiles-out", default="results/zone-quantiles.csv")
    zb.add_argument("--draws-out", default="results/zone-draws.csv.gz")
    zb.add_argument(
        "--backtest-config",
        default="packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml",
        help="Gives `[forecast]` min_horizon and max_horizon, the weeks "
        "scored.",
    )

    pst = sub.add_parser(
        "pairing-sensitivity",
        help="Score randomwalk and randomwalknowcast with no pairing and "
        "with their provinces paired by the rolling rho_p, from one "
        "forecast each, on the BDBV release backtest "
        "(`bdbvhub.pairing`); the German study is `nowcastgermany "
        "pairing-sensitivity`.",
    )
    pst.add_argument("--study", choices=["bdbv"], default="bdbv")
    pst.add_argument("--data", default=None, help="The data directory.")
    pst.add_argument(
        "--config",
        default=None,
        help="packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml.",
    )
    pst.add_argument(
        "--chunk", default=None, help=_CHUNK_HELP.format(what="origins")
    )
    pst.add_argument("--out", default="results/pairing")
    pst.add_argument(
        "--candidates",
        action="store_true",
        help="Score every copula.CANDIDATES setting instead, and print "
        "them best first (`bdbvhub.pairing.bdbv_candidates`).",
    )

    dig = sub.add_parser(
        "digest",
        help="Print a hash of what a backtest reads, to key its outputs.",
    )
    dig.add_argument("--root", default=".")
    dig.add_argument(
        "--with",
        dest="extra",
        nargs="*",
        default=[],
        help="Further files or directories the run reads.",
    )
    dig.add_argument("--text", default="", help="Such as the commands run.")
    dig.add_argument(
        "--model",
        default=None,
        help="Hash only this model's code (its import closure) with the "
        "data, for a --forecast-only run of it.",
    )

    sc = sub.add_parser(
        "score",
        help="Score the forecasts written by --forecast-only runs, every "
        "model together, and write the results as one run would.",
    )
    sc.add_argument(
        "--config", default="packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml"
    )
    sc.add_argument("--data", default=data_dir)
    sc.add_argument("--results", default="results")
    _add_store_arg(sc)
    sc.add_argument("--output", default="results")
    sc.add_argument(
        "parts",
        nargs="+",
        help="The runs' --parts directories, in the order one run takes "
        "the models.",
    )

    cat = sub.add_parser(
        "concat-results",
        help="Stack the results files of runs made apart, in the order given.",
    )
    cat.add_argument("--out", default="results")
    cat.add_argument(
        "--dedupe",
        nargs="*",
        default=[],
        help="Files every part writes in full, such as a truth table: "
        "one copy of each row is kept.",
    )
    cat.add_argument("parts", nargs="+", help="Each run's results directory.")

    fit = sub.add_parser(
        "fit", help="Fit a configuration and write its diagnostics."
    )
    fit.add_argument("--model", default="randomwalk")
    fit.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    _task_args(fit, data_dir)
    fit.add_argument(
        "--sampler-json",
        default="{}",
        help="Sampler settings as JSON (a candidate's `sampler` table).",
    )
    fit.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="Fit directory.")

    fst = sub.add_parser(
        "fit-store", help="Plan, make or load the fitted models' stored fits."
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "action", choices=["plan", "fit", "load", "unpack", "archive"]
    )
    fst.add_argument("--store", default="output/fit-store")
    fst.add_argument("--data", default=data_dir)
    fst.add_argument(
        "--config", default="packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml"
    )
    fst.add_argument("--policy", default="packages/bdbvsubmission/policy.toml")
    fst.add_argument(
        "--model", help="With `fit` or `unpack`: the model to fit or read."
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "--origin",
        help="With `fit`, `unpack` or `archive`: the real origin.",
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "--reference-date",
        default=None,
        help="With `archive`: the round, as `nowcast --reference-date`.",
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "--out",
        default=None,
        help="With `plan`: write the missing fits as a matrix JSON here. "
        "With `unpack`: the fit directory to write. "
        "With `archive`: the hub tables file to write.",
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "--origins",
        nargs="*",
        default=None,
        help="With `plan` or `load`: only these origins (default: all).",
    )
    fst.add_argument("--results", default="results")
    fst.add_argument(
        "--models",
        nargs="*",
        default=None,
        help="With `plan` or `load`: only these models (default: all "
        "fitted). With `archive`: default every candidate's model.",
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "--retry-failed",
        action="store_true",
        help="With `plan`: plan the fits stored as failed again.",
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "--usable",
        action="store_true",
        help="With `plan`: a pair with an older stored fit that `unpack` "
        "can use is not lacking.",
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "--current-only",
        action="store_true",
        help="With `load`: load only the current code's fits; a pair not "
        "yet fitted for it loads none and is listed as pending.",
    )
    fst.add_argument(
        "--keys",
        default=None,
        help="With `plan`: write every current key here, for pruning.",
    )

    plot = sub.add_parser("plot-submission", help="Plot a submitted hub file.")
    plot.add_argument("--submission", required=True)
    plot.add_argument("--vintage", default="latest")
    plot.add_argument("--data", default=data_dir)
    plot.add_argument("--out", required=True)

    prt = sub.add_parser(
        "plot-rt-submission",
        help="Plot the wk R_t rows of a submitted hub file.",
    )
    prt.add_argument("--submission", required=True)
    prt.add_argument(
        "--names",
        default=None,
        help="A CSV with `location` and `location_name`, for the titles.",
    )
    prt.add_argument("--out", required=True)

    ppc = sub.add_parser(
        "plot-ppc", help="Plot a fit's posterior predictive checks."
    )
    ppc.add_argument("--ppc", required=True, help="A ppc.json file.")
    ppc.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ppc.add_argument("--stream", default="total")

    tsn = sub.add_parser(
        "truth-sensitivity",
        help="How the truth-final constants move what is scored "
        "(nowcasteval.nowcast.truth_sensitivity), as a Markdown table.",
    )
    tsn.add_argument("--data", default=data_dir)
    tsn.add_argument(
        "--config", default="packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml"
    )
    tsn.add_argument(
        "--out", default=None, help="Markdown file; stdout if not given."
    )

    rtc = sub.add_parser(
        "rt-check",
        help="Write the Rt sense-check page of a renewal fit directory: "
        "Rt by country, province and zone over their cases.",
    )
    rtc.add_argument("--fit", required=True, help="A fit directory.")
    rtc.add_argument("--data", default=data_dir)
    rtc.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="The HTML page to write.")

    coh = sub.add_parser(
        "coherence",
        help="Compare the national data with the sum of the provinces, and "
        "each province and the country with the sum of their zones.",
    )
    coh.add_argument("--vintage", default="latest")
    coh.add_argument("--data", default=data_dir)
    coh.add_argument("--out", default=None)

docs.title: bdbvhub.submission.hub
docs.text:
Write hub submissions and model metadata.

A submission is a CSV with columns reference_date, forecast_date, target, target_end_date, location, output_type, output_type_id and value. Every count row (wk inc confirmed cases) is one week of one sample trajectory. A renewal model also gives the optional wk R_t target as quantiles (rt_table) for the weeks the round takes (rt_end_dates). forecast_date is the day the PR is opened. A resubmission in the same week keeps the file on the hub's main branch unchanged and appends rows with one new forecast_date. The round BDBV 2026 nowcasting and forecasting takes exactly 100 samples for each (reference_date, location, target), and each sample index covers the same target weeks within a location.

submission.validate checks the written files as hubValidations does. The authoritative check is still hubValidations (task bdbvhub:validate).

def model_abbr_for(model: str, path: Path | str = SUBMISSION_CONFIG) -> str:
    """Return the hub abbreviation a model submits under.

    A model with its own entry under `[models]` in
    `packages/bdbvhub/config/hub.toml` is a
    hub model of its own. Every other model submits under the
    `[submission]` abbreviation, one value not derived from a model key,
    so every renewal variant and every fallback submits under one id.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : str
        The model key, such as `"randomwalknowcast"`.
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        The configuration file.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The abbreviation, such as `"baseline"`.
    """
    with Path(path).open("rb") as fh:
        config = tomllib.load(fh)
    own = config.get("models", {}).get(model, {})
    return str(own.get("model_abbr") or config["submission"]["model_abbr"])

def to_hub_table(
    samples: pd.DataFrame,
    reference_date: dt.date | str,
    target: str = "wk inc confirmed cases",
    *,
    unassigned: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    zones: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    forecast_date: dt.date | str | None = None,
    zones_sum: bool = True,
    national: str = "sum",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Turn forecast samples into the hub's submission table.

    The table meets every guarantee in `docs/submission/hub-spec.md`:
    sample ids `1..n_samples` reused in every location, one row per id for every
    week, the same weeks for every location, whole non-negative counts
    and, by default, the national value as the sum of the provinces for
    each sample, replacing any national rows in `samples`. A model that
    forecasts the country itself (`own_national`, the Chronos-2 models)
    keeps its own national rows with `national="own"`. The hub does not
    require the sum (`docs/submission/hub-spec.md`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample` (an integer
        index, one joint draw across weeks and provinces) and `value`.
    reference_date : datetime.date or str
        The round's reference date.
    target : str
        The target name.
    unassigned : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        A modelled component of the national count not assigned to any
        province, with columns `target_end_date`, `sample` and `value`.
        It is added to the national sum. Missing rows count as zero.
    zones : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        Health-zone samples (columns as `samples`), such as from
        `nowcastbaselines.zones.zones_for_model`. They are not added to the
        national value.
    n_samples : int
        Number of samples each location must have.
    forecast_date : datetime.date or str, optional
        The day the PR is opened. The default is today (UTC), see
        `run_date`. The hub requires it to be on or before the
        reference date and within a day of the validation date.
    zones_sum : bool
        Check that the zones sum to the rounded province samples, sample
        by sample, as a split model's must. False for the random walks'
        own zone draws and the foundation models' block zones
        (`zones_need_not_sum`); the hub
        does not require the sum (its `model-output/README.md` allows
        any subset of locations).
    national : {"sum", "own"}
        `"sum"` writes each sample's national value as the sum of its
        provinces, plus `unassigned`. `"own"` writes the national rows in
        `samples` as they are, checked like any location; `unassigned`
        must then be empty.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `HUB_COLUMNS`, sorted by location, sample and week.
        Values are rounded to whole cases before the national sum, so the
        national value is exactly the sum of the written province values.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a province or zone does not have sample ids `1..n_samples`, a
        sample lacks a week, locations cover different weeks, or, with
        `zones_sum`, the zones do not sum to their provinces, or, with
        `national="own"`, `samples` has no complete national rows.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from bdbvhub.submission.hub import (
    ...     model_id, to_hub_table, write_submission
    ... )
    >>> samples = forecasts.query("model == 'randomwalknowcast'")
    >>> table = to_hub_table(samples, task.reference_date)
    >>> write_submission(table, "output/submission", model_id("rwnowcast"))
    """
    if national not in ("sum", "own"):
        raise ValueError(f"national must be 'sum' or 'own', not {national!r}.")
    ref = as_date(reference_date).isoformat()
    fdate = as_date(forecast_date or run_date()).isoformat()
    own = _tidy(samples.loc[samples["location"] == NATIONAL])
    if national == "own":
        if own.empty:
            raise ValueError("No national rows to keep (national='own').")
        if unassigned is not None and not unassigned.empty:
            raise ValueError("An unassigned component needs national='sum'.")
    prov = _tidy(samples.loc[samples["location"] != NATIONAL])
    if prov.empty:
        raise ValueError("No province samples to write.")
    zone = _zone_rows(prov, zones, zones_sum)
    ids = set(range(1, n_samples + 1))
    weeks = sorted(set(prov["target_end_date"]))
    checked = [prov, zone, own] if national == "own" else [prov, zone]
    for loc, rows in pd.concat(checked).groupby("location"):
        if set(rows["sample"]) != ids:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{loc}: sample ids must be 1 to {n_samples}, the same in "
                "every location."
            )
        if sorted(set(rows["target_end_date"])) != weeks:
            raise ValueError(f"{loc}: every location needs the same weeks.")
        if (
            len(rows) != n_samples * len(weeks)
            or rows.duplicated(["sample", "target_end_date"]).any()
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{loc}: every sample needs exactly one row for each week."
            )
    if national == "own":
        both = pd.concat([prov, own, zone], ignore_index=True)
        return _hub_rows(both, ref, fdate, target)
    national_rows = (
        prov.groupby(["target_end_date", "sample"])["value"].sum().reset_index()
    )
    if unassigned is not None and not unassigned.empty:
        extra = (
            unassigned.assign(
                target_end_date=unassigned["target_end_date"].astype(str),
                sample=unassigned["sample"].astype("int64"),
                value=unassigned["value"].clip(lower=0).round(),
            )
            .groupby(["target_end_date", "sample"])["value"]
            .sum()
        )
        national_rows = national_rows.set_index(["target_end_date", "sample"])
        national_rows["value"] = national_rows["value"].add(extra, fill_value=0)
        national_rows = national_rows.reset_index()
    national_rows["location"] = NATIONAL
    both = pd.concat([prov, national_rows, zone], ignore_index=True)
    return _hub_rows(both, ref, fdate, target)

def own_national(name: str | None) -> bool:
    """Return whether model `name` forecasts the country itself.

    The Chronos-2 models forecast the country as one series of their
    joint block, so their national draws are written as they are
    (`to_hub_table(..., national="own")`). Every other model's national
    value is the per-sample sum of its provinces.
    """
    if name is None:
        return False
    import typing

    from bdbvhub.models import list_models
    from nowcastfoundation.forecaster import FoundationModel

    specs = {s.name: s for s in list_models()}
    if name not in specs:
        return False
    # Decided from the registered factory, so no model (and no fine-tuned
    # checkpoint) is built: FoundationModel itself, or a builder of one.
    func = getattr(specs[name].factory, "func", specs[name].factory)
    if isinstance(func, type):
        return issubclass(func, FoundationModel)
    return typing.get_type_hints(func).get("return") is FoundationModel

def zones_need_not_sum(name: str | None) -> bool:
    """Return whether model `name`'s zones need not sum to its provinces.

    The random walks forecast each zone from its own data
    (`nowcastbaselines.zones.walks_own_zones`), and the foundation models take
    their zones straight from their block, as they do the provinces and

        The hub's `hub-config/tasks.json`.
    reference_date : str
        The round.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of str
        The target end dates of the `wk R_t` task open to this reference
        date, from the week before it to the reference week (the target
        takes no horizon after 0); empty if the round has none.
    """
    config = json.loads(Path(tasks_json).read_text())
    ref = as_date(reference_date)
    out: set[str] = set()
    for rnd in config["rounds"]:
        for task in rnd["model_tasks"]:
            ids = task["task_ids"]
            targets = _options(ids.get("target", {}))
            refs = _options(ids.get("reference_date", {}))
            if RT_TARGET not in targets or reference_date not in refs:
                continue
            for end in _options(ids.get("target_end_date", {})):
                if 0 <= (ref - as_date(end)).days <= 7:
                    out.add(end)
    return tuple(sorted(out))

def rt_table(
    rt: pd.DataFrame,
    reference_date: str,
    end_dates: tuple[str, ...],
    forecast_date: str | dt.date | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a fit's Rt quantiles as `RT_TARGET` rows of the submission.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rt : pandas.DataFrame
        A renewal fit's `nowcastrenewal.forecaster.RT_FILE`: `location`,
        `target_end_date`, `output_type_id` (the quantile level) and
        `value`.
    reference_date : str
        The round.
    end_dates : tuple of str
        The weeks the round takes (`rt_end_dates`); other weeks are left
        out.
    forecast_date : str or datetime.date, optional
        As in `to_hub_table`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Rows with `HUB_COLUMNS`, `output_type` `quantile`. Its
        `output_type_id` is of object dtype, so joined to the count rows
        their sample ids stay integers.
    """
    fd = as_date(forecast_date) if forecast_date else run_date()
    keep = rt.loc[rt["target_end_date"].astype(str).isin(end_dates)]
    out = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "reference_date": str(reference_date),
            "forecast_date": str(fd),
            "target": RT_TARGET,
            "target_end_date": keep["target_end_date"].astype(str),
            "location": keep["location"],
            "output_type": RT_OUTPUT_TYPE,
            # Object, so a file with integer sample ids keeps them.
            "output_type_id": keep["output_type_id"]
            .astype(float)
            .astype(object),
            "value": keep["value"].astype(float),
        }
    )
    return out.sort_values(
        ["location", "target_end_date", "output_type_id"]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)[list(HUB_COLUMNS)]

        "team_funding",
        "ensemble_of_hub_models",

Validate BDBV Modeling Hub submissions against the hub's own config.

The hub's rules are read at run time from a local clone of InsightNet-US/BDBV-Modeling-Hub (hub-config/tasks.json, hub-config/admin.json and hub-config/model-metadata-schema.json), so the validator follows config changes such as new reference dates.

Checks mirror the names used by the R package hubValidations so results can be compared one to one. Two checks are Python only and stricter than hubValidations 3.0.0: spl_id_type (sample ids must be integers when the config says so) and readme_horizon (a warning when a target_end_date is not a Saturday within the README's window).

Usage::

bdbvhub validate --hub PATH [--metadata-dir DIR]
    [--now ISO8601 | --skip-window] [--json OUT] FILE...

Exit status is 1 if any file has a failed check.

class Report:
    """The checks run on one file.

    Attributes
    ----------
    file : str
        The file checked.
    checks : list of Check
        Each check's outcome, in the order run.
    """

    file: str
    checks: list[Check] = field(default_factory=list)

    def add(
        self,
        check: str,
        ok: bool,
        message: str,
        halt: bool = False,
        fail_message: str | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Record a check that passes when `ok` is true.

        Parameters
        ----------
        check : str
            Check name, as in hubValidations.
        ok : bool
            Whether the check passed.
        message : str
            Message to record.
        halt : bool, default False
            Record a failure as `error`, which stops later checks.
        fail_message : str, optional
            Message to record instead when the check fails.

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            `ok`.
        """
        status = "pass" if ok else ("error" if halt else "fail")
        self.checks.append(
            Check(check, status, message if ok else fail_message or message)
        )
        return ok

    def skip(self, check: str, message: str) -> None:
        """Record a check that was not run.

        Parameters
        ----------
        check : str
            Check name.
        message : str
            Why it was skipped.
        """
        self.checks.append(Check(check, "skip", message))

    def warn(self, check: str, message: str) -> None:
        """Record a warning, which does not fail the file.

        Parameters
        ----------
        check : str
            Check name.
        message : str
            The warning.
        """
        self.checks.append(Check(check, "warn", message))

    @property
    def failed(self) -> list[Check]:
        """The checks with status `fail` or `error`.

        Returns
        -------
        list of Check
            The failed checks.
        """
        return [c for c in self.checks if c.status in ("fail", "error")]

    @property
    def valid(self) -> bool:
        """Whether no check failed.

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            True if the file passes.
        """
        return not self.failed

@dataclass
class Hub:
    """The hub's configuration, read from a local clone.

    Attributes
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path
        Root of the clone.
    rounds : list of Round
        The rounds in `hub-config/tasks.json`.
    admin : dict
        `hub-config/admin.json`.
    metadata_schema : dict or None
        `hub-config/model-metadata-schema.json`, if present.
    """

    path: Path
    rounds: list[Round]
    admin: dict[str, Any]
    metadata_schema: dict[str, Any] | None

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> Hub:
        """Read the hub configuration from a clone.

        Parameters
        ----------
        path : str or pathlib.Path
            Root of a clone of the hub repository.

        Returns
        -------
        Hub
            The configuration.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> from bdbvhub.submission.validate import Hub, validate_file
        >>> hub = Hub.load("../BDBV-Modeling-Hub")
        >>> report = validate_file("model-output/x/2026-11-07-x.csv", hub)
        >>> report.valid, [c.check for c in report.failed]
        """
        p = Path(path)
        tasks = json.loads((p / "hub-config" / "tasks.json").read_text())
        admin = json.loads((p / "hub-config" / "admin.json").read_text())
        schema_p = p / "hub-config" / "model-metadata-schema.json"
        schema = json.loads(schema_p.read_text()) if schema_p.exists() else None
        rounds = []
        for i, r in enumerate(tasks["rounds"]):
            mts = []
            for mt in r["model_tasks"]:
                tids = {
                    k: TaskId(
                        _vals(v.get("required")), _vals(v.get("optional"))
                    )
                    for k, v in mt["task_ids"].items()
                }
                ots = {
                    k: _parse_output_type(k, v)
                    for k, v in mt["output_type"].items()
                }
                mts.append(ModelTask(tids, ots))
            rounds.append(
                Round(
                    index=i,
                    name=r.get("round_name", f"round {i + 1}"),
                    round_id_from_variable=bool(r["round_id_from_variable"]),
                    round_id=r["round_id"],
                    model_tasks=mts,
                    submissions_due=r["submissions_due"],
                )
            )
        return cls(p, rounds, admin, schema)

    @property
    def timezone(self) -> ZoneInfo:
        """The hub's time zone, from `admin.json`.

        Returns
        -------
        zoneinfo.ZoneInfo
            The time zone, UTC if none is set.
        """
        return ZoneInfo(self.admin.get("timezone", "UTC"))

    @property
    def file_formats(self) -> list[str]:
        """The file formats the hub accepts.

        Returns
        -------
        list of str
            Such as `["csv"]`.
        """
        return list(self.admin.get("file_format", ["csv"]))

    def find_round(self, round_id: str) -> Round | None:
        """Find the round a round id belongs to.

        Parameters
        ----------
        round_id : str
            Round id, the reference date.

        Returns
        -------
        Round or None
            The round, or None if no round has that id.
        """
        for r in self.rounds:
            if round_id in r.round_ids:
                return r
        return None

    def submission_window(
        self, rnd: Round, round_id: str
    ) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
        """Open and close times of the submission window, in hub time.

        Matches hubValidations: the window opens at 00:00:00 on the start
        day and closes at 23:59:59 on the end day.

        Parameters
        ----------
        rnd : Round
            The round, from `find_round`.
        round_id : str
            Round id, the reference date.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple of datetime.datetime
            Opening and closing times.
        """
        due = rnd.submissions_due
        tz = self.timezone
        if "relative_to" in due:
            ref = date.fromisoformat(round_id)
            start_d = ref + timedelta(days=int(due["start"]))
            end_d = ref + timedelta(days=int(due["end"]))
        else:
            start_d = date.fromisoformat(str(due["start"]))
            end_d = date.fromisoformat(str(due["end"]))
        return (
            datetime.combine(start_d, time(0, 0, 0), tz),
            datetime.combine(end_d, time(23, 59, 59), tz),
        )

    >>> hub = Hub.load("../BDBV-Modeling-Hub")
    >>> report = validate_file("model-output/x/2026-11-07-x.csv", hub)
    >>> report.valid, [c.check for c in report.failed]
    """
    p = Path(path)
    tasks = json.loads((p / "hub-config" / "tasks.json").read_text())
    admin = json.loads((p / "hub-config" / "admin.json").read_text())
    schema_p = p / "hub-config" / "model-metadata-schema.json"
    schema = json.loads(schema_p.read_text()) if schema_p.exists() else None
    rounds = []
    for i, r in enumerate(tasks["rounds"]):
        mts = []
        for mt in r["model_tasks"]:
            tids = {
                k: TaskId(
                    _vals(v.get("required")), _vals(v.get("optional"))
                )
                for k, v in mt["task_ids"].items()
            }
            ots = {
                k: _parse_output_type(k, v)
                for k, v in mt["output_type"].items()
            }
            mts.append(ModelTask(tids, ots))
        rounds.append(
            Round(
                index=i,
                name=r.get("round_name", f"round {i + 1}"),
                round_id_from_variable=bool(r["round_id_from_variable"]),
                round_id=r["round_id"],
                model_tasks=mts,
                submissions_due=r["submissions_due"],
            )
        )
    return cls(p, rounds, admin, schema)

def submission_window(
    self, rnd: Round, round_id: str
) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    """Open and close times of the submission window, in hub time.

    Matches hubValidations: the window opens at 00:00:00 on the start
    day and closes at 23:59:59 on the end day.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rnd : Round
        The round, from `find_round`.
    round_id : str
        Round id, the reference date.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of datetime.datetime
        Opening and closing times.
    """
    due = rnd.submissions_due
    tz = self.timezone
    if "relative_to" in due:
        ref = date.fromisoformat(round_id)
        start_d = ref + timedelta(days=int(due["start"]))
        end_d = ref + timedelta(days=int(due["end"]))
    else:
        start_d = date.fromisoformat(str(due["start"]))
        end_d = date.fromisoformat(str(due["end"]))
    return (
        datetime.combine(start_d, time(0, 0, 0), tz),
        datetime.combine(end_d, time(23, 59, 59), tz),
    )

def validate_submission(
    file: str | Path,
    hub: Hub,
    metadata_dirs: Iterable[Path] = (),
    now: datetime | None = None,
    skip_window: bool = False,
    previous: str | Path | None = None,
) -> Report:
    """Run all model-output checks on one file.

    The hub's `forecast_date` checks run first. The standard checks then
    see only the new rows, without `forecast_date`, as in the hub's own
    workflow.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file : str or pathlib.Path
        The model-output CSV.
    hub : Hub
        The hub configuration.
    metadata_dirs : iterable of pathlib.Path
        Directories to look for the model's metadata in.
    now : datetime.datetime, optional
        Time to check the submission window against. Defaults to now.
    skip_window : bool, default False
        Skip the window check and the check that the new forecast date
        is recent.
    previous : str or pathlib.Path, optional
        The file now on the hub's main branch at the same path, if any.

    Returns
    -------
    Report
        The checks and their outcomes.
    """
    fp = Path(file)
    rep = Report(str(file))

    # File-level checks.
    meta = parse_file_name(fp.name)
    if not rep.add(
        "file_name",
        meta is not None,
        f'File name "{fp.name}" is valid.',
        halt=True,
        fail_message=f'File name "{fp.name}" must be '
        "<round_id>-<team>-<model>.<ext>.",
    ):
        return rep
    assert meta is not None
    model_id = f"{meta['team']}-{meta['model']}"
    round_id = meta["round_id"]
    rep.add(
        "file_location",
        fp.parent.name == model_id,
        "File directory name matches `model_id` in file name.",
        fail_message=f'File should be in directory "{model_id}", '
        f'not "{fp.parent.name}".',
    )
    rnd = hub.find_round(round_id)
    if not rep.add(
        "round_id_valid",
        rnd is not None,
        "`round_id` is valid.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=f'`round_id` "{round_id}" is not in '
        "hub-config/tasks.json.",
    ):
        return rep
    assert rnd is not None
    if not rep.add(
        "file_format",
        meta["ext"] in hub.file_formats,
        "File is accepted hub format.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=f'Extension "{meta["ext"]}" not in {hub.file_formats}.',
    ):
        return rep
    clock = now or datetime.now(hub.timezone)
    if clock.tzinfo is None:
        clock = clock.replace(tzinfo=hub.timezone)
    dirs = [*metadata_dirs, hub.path / "model-metadata"]
    rep.add(
        "metadata_exists",
        find_metadata(model_id, dirs) is not None,
        "Metadata file exists.",
        fail_message=f"No metadata file {model_id}.yml or .yaml.",
    )
    if skip_window:
        rep.skip("submission_time", "Submission window check skipped.")
    else:
        start, end = hub.submission_window(rnd, round_id)
        t = clock
        rep.add(
            "submission_time",
            start <= t <= end,
            "Submission time is within the submission window.",
            fail_message=f"Time {t.isoformat()} is outside window "
            f"{start.isoformat()} to {end.isoformat()}.",
        )

    # Read.
    try:
        with fp.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
            reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
            cols = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
            rows: list[Row] = [dict(r) for r in reader]
    except (OSError, csv.Error, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
        rep.add(
            "file_read",
            False,
            "",
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f"File could not be read: {e}",
        )
        return rep
    date_ids = _date_task_ids(rnd)
    bad_read = []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        if None in r or any(v is None for v in r.values()):
            bad_read.append(f"line {i}: wrong number of fields")
            continue
        v = r.get("value", "")
        if v not in NA_STRINGS and not _is_number(v):
            bad_read.append(f'line {i}: `value` "{v}" is not numeric')
        for c in date_ids & set(cols):
            if r[c] not in NA_STRINGS and not DATE_RE.match(r[c]):
                bad_read.append(f'line {i}: `{c}` "{r[c]}" is not a date')
    if not rep.add(
        "file_read",
        not bad_read,
        "File could be read.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message="File could not be read with the hub schema: "
        + "; ".join(bad_read[:5]),
    ):
        return rep

    # The hub's own forecast_date checks, then the standard ones on the
    # rows this submission adds, without that column. Files of the
    # round's first, cumulative target have neither column and are not
    # subject to them.
    if FORECAST_DATE in cols or "target_end_date" in cols:
        prev_cols: list[str] | None = None
        prev_rows: list[Row] | None = None
        if previous is not None:
            try:
                prev_cols, prev_rows = read_rows(previous)
            except (OSError, csv.Error, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
                rep.add(
                    "forecast_date_preserved",
                    False,
                    "",
                    halt=True,
                    fail_message=f"The hub's copy could not be read: {e}",
                )
                return rep
        today = None if skip_window else clock.astimezone(hub.timezone).date()
        problems, new_idx = forecast_date_problems(
            rows, cols, prev_rows, prev_cols, today
        )
        for check, message in problems:
            rep.add(check, False, "", halt=True, fail_message=message)
        if problems:
            return rep
        rep.add(
            "forecast_date",
            True,
            "`forecast_date` is valid and adds one new date.",
        )
        rows = [
            {k: v for k, v in rows[i].items() if k != FORECAST_DATE}
            for i in new_idx
        ]
        cols = [c for c in cols if c != FORECAST_DATE]

    # Round id column.
    ric = rnd.round_id
    if rnd.round_id_from_variable:
        if not rep.add(
            "valid_round_id_col",
            ric in cols,
            "`round_id_col` name is valid.",
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f'Column "{ric}" missing.',
        ):
            return rep
        ids = sorted({r[ric] for r in rows})
        if not rep.add(
            "unique_round_id",
            len(ids) == 1,
            f'`round_id` column "{ric}" has a single value.',
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f'Column "{ric}" contains {len(ids)} '
            f"values: {', '.join(ids)}.",
        ):
            return rep
        if not rep.add(
            "match_round_id",
            ids[0] == round_id,
            "`round_id` column matches the file name.",
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f"`round_id` value {ids[0]} does not "
            f'match file name "{round_id}".',
        ):
            return rep

    # Columns.
    expected = [*rnd.task_id_names, *STD_COLS]
    missing = [c for c in expected if c not in cols]
    extra = [c for c in cols if c not in expected]
    msg = []
    if missing:
        msg.append(f"Missing column(s): {', '.join(missing)}.")
    if extra:
        msg.append(f"Unexpected column(s): {', '.join(extra)}.")
    if not rep.add(
        "colnames",
        not msg,
        "Column names are valid.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=" ".join(msg),
    ):
        return rep

    # Valid values and combinations.
    mt_idx = [_row_model_task(r, rnd) for r in rows]
    bad_rows = [r for r, m in zip(rows, mt_idx, strict=True) if m is None]
    if not rep.add(
        "valid_vals",
        not bad_rows,
        "`tbl` contains valid values/value combinations.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=_invalid_values(
            bad_rows, rnd, [*rnd.task_id_names, "output_type"]
        ),
    ):
        return rep

    # Unique rows.
    key_cols = [*rnd.task_id_names, "output_type", "output_type_id"]
    keys = Counter(tuple(norm(r[c]) for c in key_cols) for r in rows)
    dups = sum(n - 1 for n in keys.values() if n > 1)
    rep.add(
        "rows_unique",
        dups == 0,
        "All task id/output type/output type id combinations are unique.",
        fail_message=f"{dups} duplicated row(s).",
    )

    _check_req_vals(rep, rows, rnd, mt_idx)
    _check_values(rep, rows, rnd, mt_idx)
    _check_non_desc(rep, rows, rnd)
    if any(r["output_type"] == "sample" for r in rows):
        _check_samples(rep, rows, rnd, mt_idx)
    else:
        for c in (
            "spl_mt_unique",
            "spl_compound_taskid_set",
            "spl_compound_tid",
            "spl_non_compound_tid",
            "spl_n",
        ):
            rep.skip(c, "No samples found.")
    _check_readme_horizon(rep, rows, round_id)
    return rep

docs.text:
Fit configurations for the automated submission workflow.

The submission CI (packages/bdbvsubmission/, see packages/bdbvsubmission/INTEGRATION.md) fits each candidate of its fallback chain with bdbvhub fit --config <name> and then forecasts from the saved fit with bdbvhub nowcast --config <name> --fit <dir>. A fit configuration says how to do both.

The chain is bvd (the renewalbvd variant), renewalsp (renewal fitted to each province on its own), main (the renewal variant), then the random walks. The renewal configurations run the PyRenew model through nowcastrenewal.forecaster.fit_renewal, which samples, draws the trajectories and writes ppc.json. The random walks need no fit: the fit store keeps their forecasts, which fit-store unpack writes into the fit directory (STORED_FORECASTS) for their configurations to read.

A fit function gets the forecast task, the sampler settings from packages/bdbvsubmission/policy.toml and the fit directory. It writes whatever the forecast needs into the directory and returns the diagnostics.json record. It may append progress lines to progress.log. The forecast function gets the task and the directory and returns province samples (columns SAMPLE_COLUMNS), optionally with an unassigned frame for a national component not assigned to any province.

def randomwalk_config(name: str, model: str = "randomwalk") -> FitConfig:
    """Build a fit configuration that runs a registered sample-free model.

    There is nothing to fit. `fit` records the task and writes
    not-applicable diagnostics and posterior predictive checks.
    `forecast` reads the stored forecasts in the fit directory
    (`STORED_FORECASTS`, `stored_forecast`), else runs the model on the
    task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The configuration name.
    model : str
        The registered model to run.

    Returns
    -------
    FitConfig
        The configuration.
    """
    reason = f"{model} has no sampler and no posterior"

    def fit(
        task: ForecastTask, sampler: Mapping[str, Any], fit_dir: Path
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        del task, sampler
        _write_json(
            fit_dir / "ppc.json", _ppc_not_available(model, name, reason)
        )
        return no_sampler_diagnostics(model, name, reason)

    def forecast(task: ForecastTask, fit_dir: Path) -> Forecast:
        stored = fit_dir / STORED_FORECASTS
        if stored.exists():
            rows = pd.read_csv(stored, dtype={"target_end_date": str})
            return stored_forecast(rows, task)
        return Forecast(get_model(model).forecast(task))

    return FitConfig(
        name=name,
        description=f"{model} model, nothing to fit",
        fit=fit,
        forecast=forecast,
        model=model,

def stored_forecast(
    rows: pd.DataFrame, task: ForecastTask, own: bool = False
) -> Forecast:
    """Return a stored forecast for the round's weeks.

    The nowcasts of earlier report dates (`as_of`) are dropped. Stored
    national rows are the model's own. A model that submits its own
    national draws (`own`, see `submission.hub.own_national`) keeps them
    as samples. For any other model, what they hold beyond the sum of the
    provinces is the national part no province holds
    (`Forecast.unassigned`), as a fit directory gives it; none if they
    hold nothing more.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rows : pandas.DataFrame
        The stored forecasts (`run_forecasts` output).
    task : ForecastTask
        The round's task, whose weeks the stored forecasts cover.
    own : bool
        Keep the national rows as samples.

    Returns
    -------
    Forecast
        The province samples and any unassigned national part.
    """
    if "as_of" in rows:
        rows = rows.loc[rows["as_of"].isna()]
    weeks = set(task.target_end_dates)
    iso = rows["target_end_date"].map(lambda d: as_date(d).isoformat())
    rows = rows.assign(target_end_date=iso)
    rows = rows.loc[rows["target_end_date"].isin(weeks), list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS)]
    national = rows["location"] == NATIONAL
    samples = rows.loc[~national].reset_index(drop=True)
    check_samples(samples, task)
    if own:
        return Forecast(rows.reset_index(drop=True))
    keys = ["target_end_date", "sample"]
    total = rows.loc[national].set_index(keys)["value"]
    summed = samples.groupby(keys)["value"].sum()
    extra = (total - summed.reindex(total.index)).clip(lower=0)
    unassigned = extra.rename("value").reset_index()
    if unassigned.empty or not (unassigned["value"] > 0).any():
        return Forecast(samples)
    return Forecast(samples, unassigned)

def run_fit(
    config: FitConfig,
    task: ForecastTask,
    sampler: Mapping[str, Any],
    fit_dir: Path | str,
    *,
    model: str,
) -> FitResult:
    """Fit a configuration and write the fit directory.

    Writes `fit.json` (the configuration, model, vintage, reference date,
    sampler settings), `diagnostics.json` and
    `progress.log`. The diagnostics are written whether or not the fit
    converged; the CI's gate judges them.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : FitConfig
        The configuration.
    task : ForecastTask
        The forecast task built from the vintage.
    sampler : mapping
        Sampler settings, the candidate's `sampler` table in
        `packages/bdbvsubmission/policy.toml`.
    fit_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        Where to write.
    model : str
        The model name the CI passed (`--model`), recorded as is.

    Returns
    -------
    FitResult
        The directory and the diagnostics.
    """
    out = Path(fit_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    progress = out / "progress.log"
    with progress.open("a") as fh:
        fh.write(f"config={config.name} vintage={task.vintage} start\n")
    start = time.monotonic()
    diag = config.fit(task, sampler, out)
    diag = write_records(
        config,
        task,
        sampler,
        out,
        model=model,
        diagnostics=diag,
        seconds=time.monotonic() - start,
    )
    with progress.open("a") as fh:
        fh.write(f"config={config.name} done\n")
    return FitResult(out, diag)

def run_forecast(
    config: FitConfig, task: ForecastTask, fit_dir: Path | str | None
) -> Forecast:
    """Forecast from a fit, checking the fit matches the task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : FitConfig
        The configuration.
    task : ForecastTask
        The forecast task.
    fit_dir : pathlib.Path or str, optional
        The fit directory written by `run_fit`. Required unless the
        configuration needs no fit, as the random walk configurations do not.

    Returns
    -------
    Forecast
        Province samples and any unassigned national component.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the fit is of another configuration or vintage.
    """
    path = Path(fit_dir) if fit_dir is not None else Path()
    if fit_dir is not None:
        record = read_fit(path)
        if record["config"] != config.name:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The fit in {fit_dir} is of config {record['config']!r}, "
                f"not {config.name!r}."
            )
        if record["vintage"] != task.vintage:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The fit in {fit_dir} is of vintage {record['vintage']}, "
                f"not {task.vintage}."
            )
    result = config.forecast(task, path)
    check_samples(result.samples, task)
    return result

Docs pages for the submitted rounds, from the submission ledger.

The submission workflow records every live round on the submission-ledger branch: state.json holds each round's outcome, and archive/<reference_date>/<run>/ holds the files of each run (the hub file, the plot, the provenance and the pull request body).

Each round records every hub model it submitted under models, keyed by hub model id, with the folder of that model's archived files. make_round_pages turns that into one page per round at docs/submission/rounds/<reference_date>.md, served at /submission/rounds/<reference_date>/, which the hub pull requests link to, with one tab per hub model id. The index is the submission log, one table per hub model id, and a snippet on the latest submission goes to the Nowcast page. A new hub model id appears without code changes.

A round's page is frozen once its hub pull request has merged: freeze_round writes it to pages/ on the ledger branch, once, and later docs builds copy that file as it is. Rounds not yet frozen are built from the ledger at each docs build.

def gh_pr_state(url: str) -> str:
    """Return a pull request's state from `gh`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    url : str
        The pull request URL.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        `open`, `closed` or `merged`.
    """
    # Over REST: the Actions token reads another org's public pull
    # request there, but not over GraphQL (`gh pr view`).
    owner, repo, _, number = url.rstrip("/").split("/")[-4:]
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["gh", "api", f"repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    if out.returncode != 0:
        msg = f"gh could not read {url}: {out.stderr.strip()}"
        raise RuntimeError(msg)
    pr = json.loads(out.stdout)
    return "merged" if pr["merged_at"] else str(pr["state"])

def make_round_pages(
    ledger: Path | str | None,
    docs: Path | str = "docs",
    generated: Path | str = "docs/generated",
    pr_state: Callable[[str], str] = gh_pr_state,
) -> list[str]:
    """Write the round pages, the submission log and the latest snippet.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ledger : pathlib.Path or str or None
        A checkout of the `submission-ledger` branch. None, or a folder
        without `state.json`, means no round has been submitted.
    docs : pathlib.Path or str
        The docs folder. Pages go to `submission/rounds/` inside it.
    generated : pathlib.Path or str
        Where the `latest-submission.md` snippet goes.
    pr_state : callable
        Returns a hub pull request's state from its URL.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        The reference dates with a page, newest first.
    """
    out = Path(docs) / "submission" / "rounds"
    if out.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    root = Path(ledger or ".")
    state = _read(root / "state.json") if ledger else {}
    rounds: dict[str, Any] = state.get("rounds", {})
    done = sorted(rounds, reverse=True)
    frozen = root / FROZEN
    for ref in done:
        if (frozen / f"{ref}.md").exists():
            for f in frozen.glob(f"{ref}*"):
                shutil.copy(f, out / f.name)
        else:
            _render(root, ref, rounds[ref], out)
    index = ["# Submission log", ""]
    if done:
        index += [
            "Every round each hub model was submitted for, newest first.",
            "The round links to its page.",
            "",
        ]
        index += _log(rounds, root, pr_state)
    (out / "index.md").write_text("\n".join(index) + "\n")
    snippet = Path(generated) / "latest-submission.md"
    snippet.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if done:
        ref = done[0]
        models = rounds[ref].get("models", {})
        each = ", ".join(
            f"{model_id} {m.get('status', '')} "
            f"({m.get('produced_by') or 'n/a'})"
            for model_id, m in sorted(models.items())
        )
        snippet.write_text(
            f"**Latest submission:** "
            f"[round {ref}](submission/rounds/{ref}.md): {each}. "
            "[Submission log](submission/rounds/index.md).\n"
        )
    else:
        snippet.write_text("")
    return done

docs.title: bdbvhub.store.store
docs.text:
The fit store: one stored fit per stored model and real origin.

The fitted models are slow, so the docs never fit them. The random walks (SAMPLE_FREE) are stored the same way, so the submission, the backtest and the docs read one forecast of each at each origin. The Fit store workflow (.github/workflows/fit-store.yml) fits each (model, origin) pair once and stores the result in the fit-store Actions artifact (bdbvhub.store.artifact), one file per fit:

<model>/<origin>/<key>.json.gz

The key (fit_key) hashes only what reaches a fit: the task at the origin, which holds only the releases up to the origin; the built model, whose representation gives its variant and resolved sampler settings; the BVDOutbreakSize release a BVD model uses; data a model reads beside the task (fit_inputs, the zone fits' zone data up to the origin); the code the model's fit can run (fit_code, without docstrings or comments, and run_forecasts), less the zone backtest; the package data files; and the runtime dependencies locked in uv.lock. A new release adds one fit per model and leaves the older ones valid, while a change to a model's code or settings refits every origin of the models that run it, and no other.

plan lists the fits the store lacks, fit makes one, and load writes the stored forecasts where the backtest and the docs read them. A submission candidate's fit also holds its fit directory (fit_files), which unpack writes out for the submission to forecast from, so the submission uses the stored fit rather than fitting again. A walk's fit directory holds its records, and unpack adds its stored forecasts (fitting.STORED_FORECASTS). A walk's stored fit also holds its run on every hub zone (walk_zones), in a file of its own beside the fit (zones_path), as it holds about 20 times the fit's rows. read_fit leaves it alone; stored_zones reads the zone runs of the fits load used, for the consumers that need them. Where the current key has not been fitted yet (pending), load uses the newest good stored fit of that pair and labels it pending (StoreStatus). Where the current key's fit failed, the model has no forecast at that origin: no older fit stands in for it. command runs bdbvhub fit-store.

def samplers(
    policy: Path | str = "packages/bdbvsubmission/policy.toml",
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return each model's NUTS settings from the CI policy.

    A stored fit uses the sampler table of the submission candidate that
    runs the same model, so the docs show the fits the submission makes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    policy : pathlib.Path or str
        The CI policy.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Sampler table by model name.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If two candidates with a sampler table run the same model, as a
        stored fit has one.
    """
    raw = tomllib.loads(Path(policy).read_text())
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for c in raw["candidates"]:
        if "model" not in c or "sampler" not in c:
            continue
        if c["model"] in out:
            msg = f"Two candidates in {policy} run {c['model']}."
            raise ValueError(msg)
        out[c["model"]] = dict(c["sampler"])
    return out

def build_model(name: str, sampler: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ForecastModel:
    """Build a registered model with its sampler table.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The model name.
    sampler : mapping
        `samplers`. A model absent from it keeps its own settings.

    Returns
    -------
    ForecastModel
        The model. The environment is left as it was.
    """
    from nowcastrenewal.forecaster import SAMPLER_ENV

    old = os.environ.pop(SAMPLER_ENV, None)
    try:
        if name in sampler:
            os.environ[SAMPLER_ENV] = json.dumps(dict(sampler[name]))
        return get_model(name)
    finally:
        os.environ.pop(SAMPLER_ENV, None)
        if old is not None:
            os.environ[SAMPLER_ENV] = old

def fit_code(model: str, root: Path | str = ".") -> list[str]:
    """List the source files a stored fit of one model can run.

    The import closure of the model's module, with any other model's
    module it builds on (`bdbvhub.store.digest.model_code`), and the
    package's data files (`STORE_DATA`), without the loader, IO and report
    modules in `KEY_SKIP`. A model with a fit directory (a renewal
    variant or a walk) also holds the code that writes its fit records
    (`RECORD_CODE`), and a walk the code of its zone run (`ZONE_CODE`).
    The store's and the
    backtest's own code is keyed by function (`FIT_FUNCTIONS`), not by
    file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : str
        A registered model.
    root : pathlib.Path or str
        The repository root.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        Paths relative to `root`, sorted.
    """
    from bdbvhub.store.digest import model_code
    from nowcastrenewal.forecaster import FIT_VARIANTS

    code = model_code(model, root, (), cli=False, skip=KEY_SKIP)
    if model in FIT_VARIANTS.values() or model in SAMPLE_FREE:
        code = sorted({*code, RECORD_CODE})
    if model in SAMPLE_FREE:
        code = sorted({*code, ZONE_CODE})
    data = [p.relative_to(root).as_posix() for p in Path(root).glob(STORE_DATA)]
    return sorted([*code, *data])

def code_digest(model: str, root: Path | str = ".") -> str:
    """Hash the code a stored fit of a model runs and its dependencies.

    Each top-level statement of the Python files in `fit_code` is hashed
    as its syntax tree, without docstrings, `__all__` or the package's own
    import lines, with the third-party imports it reads (`_code_parts`);
    other files by their name and bytes. The hashes are combined in sorted
    order, not by file, so comments, docstrings, renamed or moved modules
    and functions moved between files keep the key. The functions of the store
    and the backtest a fit runs (`FIT_FUNCTIONS`) are hashed the same
    way, read from `root`, with the Python minor version.
    The dependencies are `uv export --no-dev --all-extras --no-annotate`
    of `uv.lock`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : str
        A registered model.
    root : pathlib.Path or str
        The repository root.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        SHA-256 hex digest.
    """
    base = Path(root)
    names = fit_code(model, base)
    files: list[Path] = []
    for name in names:
        path = base / name
        files += sorted(path.rglob("*")) if path.is_dir() else [path]
    parts = []
    for path in files:
        if not path.is_file() or "__pycache__" in path.parts:
            continue
        if path.suffix == ".py":
            parts += _code_parts(path.read_text())
        else:
            body = path.name.encode() + b"\0" + path.read_bytes()
            parts.append(hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest())
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for part in sorted(parts):
        digest.update(part.encode())
    for part in _fit_functions(base):
        digest.update(part.encode())
    digest.update(repr(sys.version_info[:2]).encode())
    lock = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in ("pyproject.toml", "uv.lock"):
        lock.update((base / name).read_bytes())
    digest.update(_export(str(base.resolve()), lock.hexdigest()).encode())
    return digest.hexdigest()

def fit_key(model: ForecastModel, task: ForecastTask, code: str) -> str:
    """Hash the inputs of one stored fit.

    The task's zone data (`ZONE_FIELDS`) are hashed only for a model that
    reads them, or that the store runs on the zones (`SAMPLE_FREE`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : ForecastModel
        The model, from `build_model`, before it fits anything.
    task : ForecastTask
        The task at the origin (`origin_tasks`).
    code : str
        `code_digest`.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256 hash.
    """
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    zones = getattr(model, "reads_zones", False)
    reads_places = getattr(model, "reads_places", False)
    head = {
        "model": _settings(model),
        "code": code,
        "bvd": _bvd_tag(model, task),
    }
    # Data a model reads beside the task (the zone fits' zone data).
    inputs = getattr(model, "fit_inputs", None)
    if inputs is not None:
        head["inputs"] = inputs(task)
    digest.update(json.dumps(head, sort_keys=True).encode())
    on_zones = zones or model.name in SAMPLE_FREE
    for f in fields(task):
        if f.name in ZONE_FIELDS and not on_zones:
            continue
        if f.name in PLACE_FIELDS and not reads_places:
            continue
        value = getattr(task, f.name)
        if f.name == "places" and value is not None and not zones:
            value = value.loc[~value["location"].map(is_zone)]
        digest.update(f.name.encode())
        if isinstance(value, pd.DataFrame):
            digest.update(value.to_csv(index=False).encode())
        else:
            digest.update(repr(value).encode())
    return digest.hexdigest()[:16]

def current_keys(
    tasks: Mapping[str, ForecastTask],
    models: Sequence[str],
    sampler: Mapping[str, Any],
    code: str | Mapping[str, str],
) -> Keys:
    """Return the current key of every stored model at every origin.

    models : sequence of str
        The stored models.
    sampler : mapping
        `samplers`.
    code : str or mapping
        `code_digest`, or each model's by name.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Key by (model, origin).
    """
    built = {m: build_model(m, sampler) for m in models}
    codes = {m: code if isinstance(code, str) else code[m] for m in models}
    return {
        (m, origin): fit_key(built[m], task, codes[m])
        for origin, task in tasks.items()
        for m in models
    }

def write_fit(store: Path | str, stored: StoredFit) -> Path:
    """Write a fit to the store as gzipped JSON.

    A walk's zone run goes to its own file (`zones_path`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    store : pathlib.Path or str
        The store root.
    stored : StoredFit
        The fit.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The file written.
    """
    m = stored.meta
    path = store_path(store, m["model"], m["origin"], m["key"])
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    body = {
        "meta": m,
        **{
            name: json.loads(
                getattr(stored, name).to_json(orient="split", index=False)
            )
            for name in _TABLES
        },
        "files": stored.files,
    }
    # No timestamp in the gzip header, so the bytes depend on the content.
    with gzip.GzipFile(path, "wb", mtime=0) as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps(body).encode())
    if not stored.zones.empty:
        write_csv(
            stored.zones, zones_path(store, m["model"], m["origin"], m["key"])
        )
    return path

def read_fit(path: Path | str) -> StoredFit:
    """Read a stored fit.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        A file written by `write_fit`.

    Returns
    -------
    StoredFit
        The fit.
    """
    body = json.loads(gzip.decompress(Path(path).read_bytes()))

    def table(name: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        if name not in body:
            return pd.DataFrame()
        return pd.read_json(
            io.StringIO(json.dumps(body[name])),
            orient="split",
            dtype=False,
        )

    forecasts, fits, delays, zone_delays = (table(n) for n in _TABLES)
    return StoredFit(
        body["meta"],
        forecasts,
        fits,
        delays,
        body.get("files", {}),
        zone_delays=zone_delays,
    )

def plan(
    keys: Keys,
    store: Path | str,
    retry_failed: bool = False,
    usable: bool = False,
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """List the fits the store lacks.

    A fit that failed is stored as failed and is not planned again until
    its inputs change, unless `retry_failed`.
    With `usable`, a pair is not lacking when `unpack` can use a fit
    (`_choose`: the current key's, else, while it is pending, the newest
    good one), as the submission asks.

    Parameters
    ----------
    keys : dict
        `current_keys`.
    store : pathlib.Path or str
        The store root.
    retry_failed : bool
        Plan the fits stored as failed again.
    usable : bool
        Count an older stored fit of the pair as present.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        `model`, `origin` and `key` of each fit to make, newest origin
        first, so the Nowcast page's fits come first.
    """
    to_fit = []
    for (model, origin), key in sorted(keys.items(), key=lambda x: x[0][1])[
        ::-1
    ]:
        path = store_path(store, model, origin, key)
        redo = retry_failed and path.exists()
        if redo:
            redo = read_fit(path).meta["status"] != "ok"
        if usable and _choose(Path(store), model, origin, key)[0]:
            continue
        if not path.exists() or redo:
            to_fit.append({"model": model, "origin": origin, "key": key})
    return to_fit
